key_insight: Nano- and micro-textures in perovskite solar cells do more than trap light: they can also improve wetting, crystallinity, charge extraction, and mechanical robustness.
engineering_relevance: Texturing is a multi-functional design lever that can raise efficiency and durability in perovskite photovoltaics, with potential transfer to photodetectors and LEDs.
method: Review of recently reported texture-related effects in perovskite-based devices
Compared benefits beyond optics: film wetting, crystal quality, carrier extraction, and mechanical stability
Synthesized implications for solar cells, photodetectors, and light-emitting diodes
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a literature survey of recent texture-related studies, summarizing observed improvements in morphology, electrical performance, and flexibility rather than presenting a single new experiment.
watch_item: Texture design must be balanced with fabrication complexity and the risk that optical gains may not translate if wetting, stress, or interface quality are not well controlled.
paper_title: More than just light management -- The multiple advantages of nano- and micro-textures in perovskite solar cells
